round_1.summary: The science reproduces. On a fresh sample that includes level walking (seed 20261101: AB02/d5, AB02/i10, AB07/d5, AB01/i0), each angle channel's component 1 with the published sign fits marker angles best under the clinical convention in 8 of 8 legs. Pure counterclockwise needs a flip for pelvis and knee. Knee and ankle moment signs agree with a force-plate lever-arm estimate in 8 of 8 legs. Hip agrees in sign in 8 of 8 legs but is weak, as reported. The ankle episode, the 13 jump frames, the stride counts 86/31/29/115, the 3 ankle and 21 foot-progression census channels and the 42/8 power split all reproduce exactly. The renumbering reverses exactly. checks.name: Sign convention derivation
checks.evidence: Derived independently with x = forward, y = up and z = x cross y = the person's right side, counterclockwise positive. Thigh and shank are measured from straight down (distal end forward = +), foot from forward horizontal (toes up = +) and pelvis as PSIS->ASIS from forward horizontal (anterior tilt = clockwise = -). Joint angle = distal minus proximal: hip flexion +, knee flexion - and ankle dorsiflexion +. Internal moments act on the distal segment: hip flexor +, knee extensor + (so knee flexor -) and ankle dorsiflexor +. The conflicts with the clinical names are exactly pelvis anterior tilt, knee flexion angle and knee flexion moment, as claimed. Power is invariant. The marker data confirm the frame: markers are z-up and y-forward, right = +x = forward x up, which agrees with the person's right. The caveat that the left leg is also viewed from the right is correctly flagged by the worker.

checks.name: Per-channel transforms on a fresh sample incl. level walking
checks.evidence: Marker angles (GT->mid knee, mid knee->mid malleoli, HEE->TOE, mid PSIS->mid ASIS) were compared with the 6 component/sign candidates after a median offset. Component 1 with the published sign under the clinical convention ranked best in 8/8 legs for every channel. Median absolute residuals: pelvis 0.07-0.14 deg (opposite sign 3.1-4.3), hip 1.0-2.2 (opposite 17.8-34.3), knee 1.2-2.9 (opposite 11.3-33.2), ankle 0.40-1.39 (opposite 5.5-9.9). AB01/i0 (level) behaves the same: pelvis 0.066, hip 1.06-1.11, knee 1.22-1.37, ankle 0.40-0.60. Moments: the lever-arm internal moment (counterclockwise +) uses GRF on the foot = -(plate force), CoP in mm registered to the heel/toe markers in stance, and a plate tilt sign chosen so the mean gravity-frame horizontal force is about 0 (residual 0.0001-0.004 BW). Source component 1 correlation: ankle +0.935 to +0.980 (slope 0.72-0.85; component 1 best by correlation in 8/8); knee -0.807 to -0.956 (slope -0.95 to -1.07; component 1 best in 8/8; so the source knee moment is flexor-positive and needs x -1 under pure counterclockwise); hip +0.30 to +0.86 (sign agrees in 8/8; component 1 best by correlation only 3/8, component 2 in 5/8). Physiology agrees: the source ankle in the last 40% of stance is -1.0 to -1.5 N*m/kg (plantarflexor negative); the source hip is -0.25 to -1.0 in early stance and +0.4 to +0.6 in late stance (flexor-positive pattern). Conclusion: transforms as claimed. Hip remains weak, as the worker states.

checks.name: Ankle episode AB07/i10 right
checks.evidence: |c2| > 90 deg on non-zero frames gives 5429 frames in two runs, 0-based [11703, 14987] and [14990, 17133]. These equal the worker's 1-based [11704, 14988] and [14991, 17134]. For (c1+180, 180-c2, c3+180), the maximum matrix difference from the raw triple is 1.28e-15 in all 6 Cardan orders; c1+180 alone gives 2.00. Re-expressed inside p1-p99 is [-16.6, 27.0], [1.1, 6.1], [-24.2, -3.4] against outside [-15.9, 27.8], [0.5, 6.3], [-24.9, -0.5], identical to the claim. Frame-to-frame orientation steps over 20 deg: 13 frames, the same set in yxz, xyz and zyx, equal to the worker's 1-based list minus 1. The p95 step inside the window is 2.4 deg. Stride accounting from RHS: 122 heel-strike pairs = 86 clean + 31 inside + 5 duration-screened (including a 14775-15724 gap that holds jump frames 14931-14991). Jump frames fall in 2 inside strides, so 29 re-expressable strides and option counts 0/86/115 are correct. The run ends where (0,0,0) zero fill begins (from 17135, 1-based). Caveat for wording (fix 5): the matrix identity holds for any triple by construction, so it is not evidence that the re-expressed values are right. The evidence is the distribution match and the small inside steps.

checks.name: Census and power storage
checks.evidence: Full independent scan, not a sample: 500 joint-angle channels have alternate-branch frames in FootProgress 21, Ankle 3 and Pelvis/Hip/Knee 0. The ankle channels are AB05/d10 L (5 frames), AB06/d5 R (8) and AB07/i10 R (5429). AB05/d10 L is a pass through the c2 ~ 90 deg singularity with c1 50-114 deg, and re-expression gives -130 to -66, so neither branch is plausible: a glitch. AB06/d5 R is a ramp to c2 = 165 just before zero fill: a glitch. I agree that only one real branch episode exists. Power: 300 channels; components 1 and 2 are all zero in exactly AB03/i10, AB04/d10, AB04/d5, AB04/i5, AB05/d10, AB05/d5, AB05/i0 and AB05/i10, giving 8 layout-2 and 42 layout-1 recordings with no mixed recording. Sign: in AB02/i0 R, component 1 correlates -1.000 with M1 x dtheta1/dt (ankle and knee); in AB05/i0 R, component 3 correlates +0.997 (ankle) and +0.963 (knee).
